newsitem.title: USA: Hudson Foods recall not seen hurting EPS -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Hudson Foods recall not seen hurting EPS -analysts.

text.p: Last week's recall of 1.2 million pounds of frozen hamburger patties produced by Hudson Foods Inc will have little impact on the meat processor's earnings, analysts said.
"From an earnings perspective, a drop of a nickel in the price of corn will mean more to Hudson than the entire hamburger division," said Merrill Lynch analyst Leonard Teitelbaum.
However, the recall due to possible E. coli bacterium contamination does present an image problem for Hudson, which is a major poultry producer.
"I think it's obviously an image problem," said William Leach, an analyst with Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette. But he said he still recommends the stock for purchase.
Hudson officials were not immediately available for comment on the possible earnings impact.
Hudson said Sunday that the recalled ground beef products accounted for less than one percent of its total sales.
Leach added that Hudson Foods' beef business in total has about $100 million in annual sales. In fiscal 1996, Hudson Foods' annual sales were $1.4 billion.

Since the recalled hamburger was processed at Hudson's plant in early June, Leach said it was likely that much of the meat had already been consumed. Health officials blamed the beef and the microbe for 16 cases of illness in Colorado in July.
"From a stock standpoint, it's been overdone," Leach said.
Hudson Foods shares at midday Monday were off 1/2 at 14-3/8.
